findings.where: case (value, statement, loci); rho; translation rows 1-2; KO 1-8; P section 'First in composition'
findings.finding: The witness ruling on the first sense (priority of composition) does not hold on the defining papers. The papers place the priority thesis inside the field's ontology: a book with a composition date and dependency relations, argued by the field's own evidence. #202 situates itself 'within an existing minority scholarly tradition'. #1217 says it 'builds on' Robinson and Gentry and 'extends them'. #542 IX.2 calls it falsifiable by historical-critical, linguistic and archaeological evidence, and IX.3 reads Robinson and Gentry as 'approaches to the void from within the opposing field'. #1101 §2.4 lists 'Near-miss positions': Baur's Tübingen school, which granted Revelation 'priority within the NT'. #1101 §3.1 records Ford's thesis that the core of Revelation (4-11) was composed by John the Baptist or his disciples, which puts that core before every other NT text. What the papers call absent ('The field cannot say that Revelation was written first', #1101 §10.1; 'organized around not stating it', #542) is a proposition the field does not assert. The papers do not say the ontology is one the field lacks. A contrary date or a reversed dependency is a contradiction inside one ontology, which §1.2a composes under P_coh. The same goes for #1420, which says canonical position served as evidence in the dating argument. That is a claim about the field's reasoning on the field's object. F1 itself says 'canonically', so translation row 1 translates F1 into what F1 already states. Under §0.10 the witness law 'does not apply where the field holds the ontology, however marginally', so this sense is the equal-terms case. A reader of the same papers would decide equal terms here, because the papers' own verb is 'extends'.
findings.evidence: #1217 In-Body Provenance Capsule: "The thesis builds on Robinson (Redating the New Testament, 1976) and Gentry (Before Jerusalem Fell, 1989), extends them with the literary-genetic argument" / #542 IX.2: "It is falsifiable (it makes specific claims about composition that could be addressed through historical-critical, linguistic, and archaeological evidence)" / #542 IX.3: "these are not support nodes for T but approaches to the void from within the opposing field" / #1101 §2.4: "The Tübingen school (F.C. Baur, 1830s–1860s) was the last major scholarly movement to date Revelation early (late 60s) and to grant it priority within the NT" / #1101 §3.1: "Ford proposed that the core of Revelation (chapters 4–11) was composed by John the Baptist or his disciples, with later Christian additions." / F1: "is canonically the last book of the New Testament."
findings.fix: Record case = equal terms on this sense: ρ = extends, with R202-01/R202-05 composed against F9, F39 and F28 under P_coh (both carried, each with its source). Re-mark translation row 1 (F1) 'untranslated: composed as received beside R202-01, R542-03, R1420-01, R1420-02'. Replace the case statement's clause 'On two senses it supplies an ontology it states no other source makes available: priority of composition ...' with: 'On priority of composition the archive argues a contrary date and a reversed dependency within the field's ontology (#202 'situated within an existing minority scholarly tradition'; #1217 'extends them'); the field holds early-composition readings marginally (#1101 §2.4 Baur; §3.1 Ford), so §0.10 does not apply.' KO text needs no change for this sense.

findings.where: case (second witness sense: the named author); rho; translation row 2; KO 13; P section 'The named author'
findings.finding: This is the closer call, but the defining papers still show the field holding, at least marginally, the ontology at issue: that 'John' is not one discrete historical individual per name. #1217 says the field 'lacks the concept', yet #1101 §3.1 lists field positions that already break the one-name-one-individual premise: Elder against Apostle (Dionysius, Eusebius, 'those who separate the Johannine corpus into multiple authors'); 'Pseudonymous. The "John" is a literary fiction'; 'Composite work. Multiple authors or redactional layers' (Charles); and Ford's Baptist core. #1101 §10.2 itself names pseudonymity as 'the closest concept'. #68's own sentence ('across multiple authors operating under a shared named position') restates the field's Johannine community/school position. #542 IX.3 cites that literature (Hengel, The Johannine Question; Smalley, John's Revelation and John's Community), and so does the field pool (F24 Dionysius, F34 John the Elder). The archive's own instruments also stand inside that ontology: #1570 M19 reports 'Dionysius replicated', and #1569 §47 says its lens cannot separate 'A school inheriting a transmission programme' from identity. What the archive adds is a refinement on the field's object: heteronymy as non-deceptive operational authorship, and the Johns as differentiated positions of one aperture-function. That is ρ = extends, a sense the field lacks on an ontology it holds. A reader could rule witness on #1217's 'historical-individual frameworks cannot parse', but §0.10's 'however marginally' tips the decision to equal terms. A ruling either way should cite #1101 §3.1.
findings.evidence: #1101 §3.1: "7. **Pseudonymous.** The "John" is a literary fiction. Argued by some modern scholars"; "8. **Composite work.** Multiple authors or redactional layers. R.H. Charles argued for significant editorial work on an underlying text."; "Modern scholars who hold this view include those who separate the Johannine corpus into multiple authors." / #1101 §10.2: "The closest concept is pseudonymity, which implies deception." / R68-01: "The Johannine community produced texts attributed to "John" — Gospel, Epistles, Revelation — across multiple authors operating under a shared named position." / #1569 §47: "A school inheriting a transmission programme fills the same slots, and the six-slot lens cannot separate inheritance from identity" / R1570-01: "**M19 — Dionysius replicated.**"
findings.fix: Record ρ = extends on the named author, unless the operator rules otherwise on #1101 §3.1. Re-mark translation row 2 'untranslated: composed as received beside R1217-10, R68-01, R683-02, R1570-01, R1217-11', and keep its located receiving texts as a provenance note. If the operator keeps the witness ruling, add #1101 §3.1 (items 2, 7, 8) to the case loci with the reason the ruling sets them aside.

summary: The row passes on translation (43/43 field claims, received quotes verbatim, receiving Greek verbatim in the seated Nestle 1904) and on KO coverage (244/244 claims, no cuts), but the mixed case does not hold on its own defining papers. The priority-of-composition sense sits inside the field's ontology: #202 'situated within an existing minority scholarly tradition', #1217 'extends them', #1101 §2.4 lists near-miss positions (Baur's priority, Ford's Baptist core). The named-author sense meets field positions recorded in #1101 §3.1 (Elder, pseudonymous, composite), F24/F34, #1569 §47 and #1570 M19. Under §0.10's 'however marginally', both senses are equal terms with ρ = extends. Translation rows 1-2 become untranslated. Remaining work: force and attribution in the P compression (Pearl, Sevens, Convergence, dropped limits, unsourced field items), KO 8's lowered 'favors', and KO 28's misstated #1569 withdrawal.
